title: Brent Crude Spikes to $109/Barrel — Highest in Four Months — as Hormuz Attacks and Houthi Port Seizure Rattle Markets
detail: Brent crude surged as high as $109.20/barrel intraday Thursday — its highest level in nearly four months — before easing to close the session up more than 6% around $107.6/barrel; WTI crude jumped 6.7% to close at $102.48/barrel, its highest since mid-May. The rally was driven by the IRGC's claimed strikes on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz a day earlier (including two attempted hits on US Navy ships), compounded by Iran-aligned Houthi rebels seizing control of Yemen's Red Sea port of Mocha, further threatening regional shipping routes. President Trump's remark in Dallas that he was 'not looking for a deal with Iran' also weighed on sentiment. Analysts said the jump raised expectations of near-term inflation pressure from energy costs.

title: IAEA Discloses Cameras Disabled, Inspectors Blocked From All Iranian Nuclear Sites Except Bushehr Since War Began
detail: A day after the Board of Governors' referral of Iran to the UN Security Council, CNN reported further detail underlying IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi's findings: the agency has been unable to visit any Iranian nuclear facility other than the Bushehr power plant since the war began Feb 28, breaking its 'continuity of knowledge' over Iran's enriched-uranium stockpile, with monitoring cameras at several sites reported disabled or inaccessible. Iran's Atomic Energy Organization chief Mohammad Eslami has said the IAEA cannot inspect sites 'until it develops specific criteria and protocols' for facilities damaged by US/Israeli strikes — a position Grossi has called a serious blow to verification capability.
